QF.id: XIII Trading, Clearing, Settlement and Risk Management_45

question.text: Under SEBI regulations, how is the Market Wide Position Limit (MWPL) for equity derivative contracts on an individual security defined?

answer.text: MWPL is 20% of the number of shares held by non-promoters (i.e. 20% of the free-float shares), expressed in number of shares
MWPL is 20% of the total (not free-float) market capitalization of the underlying stock
MWPL is 10% of the free-float market capitalization, ensuring derivatives markets remain smaller than the cash market
MWPL is determined by the exchange based on historical trading volumes, with no fixed percentage

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook defines MWPL for individual securities as 20% of the number of shares held by non-promoters, i.e. 20% of the free-float in number of shares. This caps the aggregate open interest across all exchanges in derivative contracts on that stock. The Trap: MWPL is measured in NUMBER OF SHARES, not in rupee market-capitalization terms. It is based on the free-float (non-promoter holdings), not total market cap, and the 20% figure is fixed by SEBI, not set by exchanges. Note: Free-float excludes promoter holdings, government holdings and other locked-in strategic stakes. A higher promoter holding means a smaller free-float and therefore a lower MWPL in absolute share terms.
